title: Make review navigation and status easier to read
summary: Follow the first-focus skip path from shared navigation into every main landmark, then review the queued-comment copy repair, dark-tab contrast, and 320px chrome containment. Finish with the deterministic keyboard replay, regression contracts, and regenerated browser assets.

intent.goal: Make the app's review surfaces easier to navigate, read, and trust across keyboard, assistive-technology, dark-theme, and narrow-screen use.
intent.design: One shared skip link targets focusable main landmarks, the review engine updates a whole owned count label instead of a fragile sibling text node, and two measured CSS corrections raise inactive-tab contrast while containing the 320px chrome without shrinking touch targets.
nonGoals: Deliberately preserves the Signal and Thread-Ledger visual language instead of reskinning the product.
Deliberately keeps the live imperative review engine authoritative rather than replacing its review semantics with a second component runtime.

hotspots.reason: Chromium keyboard replay proves first focus and destination focus, but physical VoiceOver and Switch Control navigation were not replayed.
The 320px correction was measured in Chromium with the current English tab labels; longer future localization would need another containment pass.

storyScope.reviewerNote: This story owns skip navigation, comment-count copy, contrast, narrow review chrome, their proof, and atlas replay. Generated dist assets are listed as excluded because the app's bounded review omits generated paths; recoverable repository removal is reviewed separately in recoverable-repository-removal.json.

steps.title: Shared navigation makes content the first keyboard escape
steps.why: Start here: persistent chrome now begins with a visually hidden-until-focused link that uses logical positioning, a strong focus ring, and one conventional main-content target.

beats.text: Start here: keyboard users receive a standard same-page link before the wordmark, breadcrumbs, theme control, and page actions.
The shared Nav mounts that link first, so every front-door screen gets the same escape without duplicating focus behavior.

steps.title: Scope selection exposes a focusable main destination
steps.why: The shared link lands on the exact scope content owner, and negative tab index lets the browser move focus there without adding main to ordinary tab order.

beats.text: The scope page gives the shared target a real main landmark and programmatic focus, so skipping chrome changes both scroll position and keyboard context.

steps.title: Review history shares the same content destination
steps.why: The saved-review list now receives the same focusable landmark contract as scope selection, avoiding a page-specific shortcut vocabulary.

beats.text: Review history reuses the exact destination id and focus behavior, keeping the first keyboard escape predictable between front-door screens.

steps.title: Live review wires the skip link without changing engine ownership
steps.why: The hand-built review chrome imports and mounts the shared link, then marks its existing main owner as the destination without moving any engine-managed view content.

beats.text: The review page adds the same first-focus escape immediately before its custom chrome while leaving the engine-owned document beneath it unchanged.

steps.title: Queued-comment copy has one engine-owned text target
steps.why: That closes the navigation path. The review summary now marks the whole count phrase, giving the imperative engine one stable node instead of asking it to rewrite a React-created sibling text node.

beats.text: The server-rendered count and noun become one deliberately owned target, so later engine refreshes can replace the complete phrase atomically.

steps.title: Count refresh replaces the whole phrase and cannot duplicate its noun
steps.why: The engine now writes one complete singular or plural phrase, eliminating the leftover React text node that produced commentscomments after a refresh.

beats.text: The refresh path replaces one marked node with the full count phrase, so React's original plural text cannot survive beside a partial engine update.

steps.title: Inactive dark review tabs clear the normal-text contrast floor
steps.why: Measured dark inactive tabs move from the dim token to the muted token, raising the composited contrast from 4.40:1 to 5.38:1 while keeping active hierarchy intact.

beats.text: The inactive tab keeps its subdued role but now clears normal-text contrast on the real translucent chrome background, while hover and active states remain unchanged.

steps.title: The 320px chrome fits without shrinking its theme target
steps.why: At the supported floor, redundant gutters collapse and the theme button drops only its extra pseudo-element slop; the visible control remains 44px and horizontal scroll disappears.

beats.text: The narrowest breakpoint spends the final pixels on labels and real controls by removing only redundant chrome gaps and padding.
Because the theme button is already 44px here, clipping its extra invisible slop removes overflow without reducing the actual touch target.

steps.title: Browser replay proves first focus and destination focus
steps.why: That closes the CSS fixes; the deterministic review replay now fails unless Tab reaches Skip to content first and Enter focuses the main landmark with the matching hash.

beats.text: The replay uses real keyboard input and inspects both ends of the interaction, preventing a visually present link with the wrong tab order or inert destination from passing.

steps.title: Scope-page contract pins the shared skip path
steps.why: The focused source test requires the target href, visible label, shared Nav adoption, and focusable scope main as one contract.

beats.text: This proof fails if either side drifts: the shared link and scope landmark must keep the same id and focus semantics.

steps.title: History contract keeps its focusable destination
steps.why: Review history gets its own guard because a future markup cleanup could otherwise leave the shared skip link pointing nowhere on this route.

beats.text: The history proof pins the main target independently, so one front-door surface cannot silently fall out of the shared keyboard contract.

steps.title: Review contracts pin navigation, copy ownership, and 320px targets
steps.why: The live review source guards join the skip destination and whole-label count update with the exact narrow breakpoint and retained 44px theme target.

beats.text: The first assertion block keeps the review skip path and full count-label ownership connected across React and the imperative engine.
The second block rejects a 320px workaround that restores overflow or shrinks the theme target below its mobile contract.
